title: Course Feedback
instructions: Please answer each question in a few sentences. Your honest feedback helps improve this course.
questions: Which topic in this course did you find most challenging, and why?
Describe one concept you understood only after the practical assignments. What made it click?
How has your approach to designing databases or APIs changed since the start of the trimester?
What would you improve about how this course was taught or assessed?
How do you plan to apply what you learned in this course going forward?
answers: Concurrency was the hardest topic. I found it difficult to see how two requests arriving at the same moment could both pass a check and break a rule. It made sense once I understood that the database has to enforce the rule itself, with a UNIQUE index and a row lock.
Transactions only made sense once I built the cancellation. The refund and the status change have to succeed or fail together, and writing it in one UPDATE inside a transaction made that click.
I used to check rules only in JavaScript. Now I put rules in the database too, with constraints, and I design the tables first so each fact is stored once.
I would add more guided practice on concurrency and queues before the assignment, and a short worked example of a transaction with a rollback.
I plan to use these skills on the backend projects I build next, especially validation, error handling, and keeping the database as the source of truth.
